content:
sam: Anyone know where to find metrics for WS streaming chunk timing? We're getting reports of partial responses and abrupt disconnects from a few customers. ticket #3456

laura: Check Grafana -> Streaming / WebSocket Latencies dashboard. There are panels for chunk p50/p95/p99 and "inter-chunk gap" histogram. URL: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/streaming-ws (team-only) :eyes:

sam: I can see p95 looks fine overall but the inter-chunk gap tail is weird for region eu-west. How do I correlate that with disconnect reasons?

tom: Use traces in Honeycomb — instrument 'ws.connection' spans and look for child spans named 'ws.send_chunk' and 'ws.close'. You can filter traces where span.duration or an `error` tag is present. Example Honeycomb query:
```
dataset=redwood_traces
where span.name = \"ws.connection\" and error = true
group by trace_id
fields span.tags.ws_close_code, span.tags.model, span.duration_ms
```
That'll show problematic sessions.

rachel: Also check Datadog logs. We add `ws_close_code` and `last_chunk_seq` to logs. Try this logs query for close codes and counts:
```
service:websocket @ws_close_code:* | top @ws_close_code by count
```
If you see a lot of 1006/1011 around the same time as the chunk-gap tail, it's a server-side issue.

maya: Don't forget LB timeouts and proxy heuristics. Partial responses can be client-side timeouts, proxy idle timeouts, or our send stalls. LB logs live in infra logging: https://logs.redwood.internal/lb/streaming (ask eng-sre for access)

sam: Can we add an alert for spikes in partial responses? Current alert only covers full connection failures. Partials are noisy for product.

observability-bot: Suggestion: add an alert "streaming.partial_response_rate" that fires when (sum(streaming.partial_responses,5m) / sum(streaming.completed_responses,5m)) > 0.005 for 5m. Include tags: {region, model}. See runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/streaming-partial-responses

laura: +1. Also let's add a histogram panel for `chunk_interarrival_ms` (bucketed) and tag by model and region so we can see which combos produce long gaps. I'll open a PR to the Grafana dashboard and add the panel. I'll also add a debug pod label `streaming.debug=true` that will flip on verbose traces for repro sessions.

sam: Laura — can you also ping eng-sre to check LB idle timeout settings? Might be the simplest fix.

tom: On disconnects, check the close codes: client-initiated 1001/1000 vs abrupt 1006 (no close frame). Server errors may be 1011. We should also log `last_chunk_size` and `last_outgoing_seq` on close. I'll make a small PR to add those fields to the standard websocket log line. Example log format we already emit:
```
{"ts":"...","svc":"websocket","user_id":"...","conn_id":"...","ws_close_code":1006,"last_chunk_seq":42,"last_chunk_size":1024}
```
That helps correlate disconnects to stalled sends.

rachel: I'll draft alert PRs: grafana panel PR (#412), logs parser update PR (#413), alert rule PR (#414). Will link when ready.

deploy-bot: deploy: grafana/dashboard/streaming-ws updated to canary (sha: a1b2c3) :rocket:

sam: Nice. Next steps: Laura adds dashboard panel + PR, Tom adds log fields + PR, Rachel wires alert & runbook update, and I'll follow up in ticket #3456 with traces we find. If anyone reproduces locally, enable `streaming.debug=true` on the pod and paste Honeycomb trace id here. Thanks! :pray:
